blocks.text:
## Highlights of the journey

The country's central region introduces coffee and volcanoes. At the Doka coffee plantation, you will discover the entire process of producing Costa Rican Arabica coffee before visiting the Poás Volcano crater and La Paz Waterfall Gardens.

Tortuguero reveals Costa Rica's Caribbean side. Travel here is largely by water: boats follow rivers and natural channels through jungle where herons, caimans, iguanas and howler monkeys may be seen.

The Arenal area combines volcanic landscapes with the Tabacón thermal springs. Another nature-focused day takes you to the Río Celeste in Tenorio National Park.

Monteverde introduces the cloud forest. The programme includes hanging bridges and a canopy zip-line tour above the treetops.

On the Pacific coast, the route follows the Tárcoles River, Manuel Antonio National Park, the Osa Peninsula and Corcovado. A separate day is devoted to a marine excursion to Caño Island, with snorkelling and opportunities to observe marine wildlife.

The final days are spent at Playa Conchal, staying at The Westin Reserva Conchal, an All-Inclusive Golf Resort & Spa.

## How the landscapes change along the route

One of this itinerary's distinctive features is that the natural environment changes almost every one or two days. Around San José and Doka, the focus is on highland coffee-growing country. The route then rises towards Poás, with its cooler volcanic climate, before entering La Paz's humid rainforest.

Tortuguero feels entirely different. Roads give way to waterways: rivers and canals become the principal routes, boats move alongside dense vegetation and much of the wildlife watching takes place from the water.

Near Arenal, the landscape changes again. Volcanic slopes, old lava fields and hot springs lie beside tropical rainforest. An evening at Tabacón means bathing in thermal pools naturally heated by volcanic activity.

Río Celeste and Tenorio add another striking contrast. This part of the journey is known for its vivid turquoise water, especially near Los Teñideros and the waterfall. Trails pass through humid forest with vines, ferns and tall trees.

At higher altitude, Monteverde has persistent moisture and mist. Mosses, orchids and giant ferns cover the trees, while hanging bridges let you experience the forest at canopy level. The canopy tour follows cables and platforms above the upper vegetation.

The journey then gradually reaches the Pacific Ocean. On the Tárcoles River, the wildlife programme moves back onto the water, now with opportunities to observe large American crocodiles and birds.

Manuel Antonio brings rainforest and sea together. Trails weave through jungle towards beaches, mangrove areas and coastal coral habitats.

Corcovado and the Osa Peninsula form the wildest portion of the route: primary forests, mangroves, secluded beaches and exceptionally diverse wildlife. Jaguars, tapirs, scarlet macaws, sloths and all four monkey species found in Costa Rica inhabit the region.

Caño Island shifts the focus from land to sea. Rays, turtles and schools of tropical fish can be encountered in clear waters around the island. Humpback whales can sometimes be seen in the region during their migration season.

The final stay at Playa Conchal is almost entirely devoted to relaxation. The shore is covered in pale, finely crushed shells, the water is clear and the programme becomes flexible after an itinerary rich in transfers and nature excursions.

## Travel format and accommodation

The tour provides English-speaking guide services, transfers, excursions along the route and accommodation in hotels across several regions.

Accommodation along the route:

- Marriott Costa Rica Hacienda Belén — Deluxe room, BB / breakfast.
- Manatus Hotel — Deluxe room, breakfast, lunch and dinner.
- Nayara Springs — Casita Deluxe, BB / breakfast.
- Sendas Monteverde — Superior room, BB / breakfast.
- Arenas del Mar Beachfront & Rainforest Resort — Rainforest Suite, BB / breakfast.
- Copa del Árbol — Luxury accommodation, breakfast, lunch and dinner.
- The Westin Playa Conchal Resort & Spa — Deluxe Garden Junior Suite, AI / all-inclusive.

Meal arrangements vary by region. City hotels and several nature lodges include breakfast. In Tortuguero and the Corcovado area, full board is provided on the specified days. The final beach resort operates on an all-inclusive basis.

The inclusion of domestic flights requires confirmation when the quotation is prepared: flights appear in the itinerary but are not separately listed under the programme's included services.

The most convenient season for this journey is generally December to April, when rainfall is less frequent and access to the national parks is often easier.

## Hotels as part of the route

Marriott Costa Rica Hacienda Belén is used during the city portion of the itinerary, with Deluxe accommodation and breakfast.

Manatus Hotel serves the nature-focused Tortuguero portion; breakfast, lunch and dinner are included.

In the Arenal area, the itinerary uses Nayara Springs, in a Casita Deluxe room on a bed-and-breakfast basis.

In Monteverde, accommodation is at Sendas Monteverde, in a Superior room with breakfast.

In Manuel Antonio, accommodation is at Arenas del Mar Beachfront & Rainforest Resort, in a Rainforest Suite with breakfast.

For the Corcovado area, the itinerary uses Copa del Árbol in the Luxury category, again including breakfast, lunch and dinner.

The final resort, The Westin Playa Conchal Resort & Spa, offers all-inclusive accommodation in a Deluxe Garden Junior Suite.

Together, these properties reflect the itinerary's progression: city hotels, lodges and resorts close to protected natural areas, then several free days by the ocean.

## Activities and physical effort

The programme combines many types of activity: road transfers, boat journeys, walks, hanging bridges, canopy zip lines, thermal springs, opportunities for seaplane sightseeing, snorkelling and marine excursions.

Activity levels vary. Some city and beach days are relatively relaxed, while the nature-focused days in Tortuguero, Monteverde, Manuel Antonio and Corcovado can be long and active.

The Río Celeste excursion follows forest trails and is not a technical mountain ascent.

At Arenal, the Los Tucanes trail passes over old lava flows.

In Monteverde, hanging bridges are combined with a canopy zip-line tour.

On the Tárcoles River, most wildlife watching takes place from a boat.

In Manuel Antonio, the programme includes a walk through the national park to the beach.

At Corcovado, one day involves travel along the Sierpe River and coast, followed by a jungle hiking day.

Caño Island offers snorkelling and diving opportunities.

The final three days at Playa Conchal allow a lighter pace: choose kayaking, snorkelling, spa treatments or simply relaxing beside the ocean.
